name: GIAC Security Essentials

fee.note: USD, excluding applicable sales tax. Practice tests are sold separately (US$399 each); a retake is US$899 and a 45-day extension US$479.

exam.format: One proctored web-based exam: 106 questions in 4 hours, remotely through ProctorU or at a Pearson VUE test centre, with CyberLive hands-on lab testing described on the exam page. Open book for printed material only. The attempt must be completed within 120 days of activation.

scope: Hands-on security essentials: access control and passwords, network architecture and protocols, cryptography, Linux and Windows security, AWS and Azure operations, endpoint and web security, incident handling, logging and SIEM, and vulnerability scanning.
ai_policy: GIAC exams are open book for printed books and notes only (no digital items or extra devices). Its exam integrity policy forbids copying exam content into any web-based location, including AI sites such as ChatGPT.
caveats: GIAC lists 26 exam objectives without weights, so no domain split is given here.
The 72% passing score applies to exam versions released on or after 6 April 2026; GIAC says to confirm the format and passing score for your attempt in your GIAC account.
The exam page describes CyberLive hands-on testing but does not say how many items are hands-on.
Renewal every four years: 36 CPE credits or a retake, plus the US$499 renewal fee (US$249 for additional renewals within two years of a full-price renewal).

prep.title: GIAC practice tests
prep.note: US$399 each; the question bank is limited, so questions can repeat.
